quotes.text: Sandbox testing is available with any Radar plan. To use the API in live mode, you must have Radar Plus or Radar Pro. Live mode is limited to 4,000 requests per month.
The `business_url` field is the only required field for an entity-less evaluation.
These are thin events: `data` is always `{}`. Use `related_object.id` to fetch the related signal or evaluation.
You can retrieve account signals and account evaluations for up to 90 days after creation.
Reserved URLs only work in a sandbox. Live mode always performs a real website evaluation.

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/radar/fraudulent-website documents an on-demand evaluation for a Connect platform, either for an existing connected account or a prospective business with a business URL. The examples use /v2/signals/account_evaluations, 2026-10-28.preview, requested_signals and account_details (new raw lines 15-59). Stripe sends a thin website-ready event or a completion event for multiple requested signals; the platform fetches results by related_object.id within the documented 90-day retrieval window. Invalid or unreachable URLs yield unknown with an explanation (new raw lines 61-130). Sandbox is available on any Radar plan, while live use requires Plus or Pro and is limited to 4,000 requests monthly (new raw lines 9-13). The May guide and source-stripe-radar-account-risk-signals.md use the earlier core namespace, request fields and result-bearing webhook description (old raw lines 10-64).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/fraudulent-website, the substantive November changes are the signals endpoint and request shape, 2026-10-28.preview example, thin per-signal and aggregate notifications, up-to-90-day retrieval, live Plus/Pro quota and sandbox-only deterministic results (new raw lines 9-70 and 169-210). Preserve the May 2026-03-25.preview core request and core-ready event separately in source-stripe-radar-account-risk-signals.md (old raw lines 10-64). Keep the existing-versus-prospective account distinction, unknown result and separate operator actions. The new action destination is a navigation change; the expanded request and response examples illustrate the revised contract and do not confer account access (old raw lines 66-68; new raw lines 72-121 and 212-214). Preserve the reciprocal Stripe Radar concept route and the distinct merchant fraud and delinquency raw routes.
